a.text: 'Universe'.
How should we interpret this word? With mathematics, physics, faith, imagination—

spans.text: How should we interpret this word? With mathematics, physics, faith, imagination—

a.text: We exhausted our minds attempting to define this still unfamiliar word in a variety of languages, and arrogantly claimed to have mastered true 'knowledge'.

spans.text: We exhausted our minds attempting to define this still unfamiliar word in a variety of languages, and arrogantly claimed to have mastered true 'knowledge'.

a.text: So why are most of us silent when destruction is so near?

spans.text: So why are most of us silent when destruction is so near?

a.text: You cannot turn back from knowledge. Since we have glimpsed the partial truths of countless fallacies, it is only natural that we cannot retreat into the darkness of ignorance, and ignore the advent of the end.

spans.text: You cannot turn back from knowledge. Since we have glimpsed the partial truths of countless fallacies, it is only natural that we cannot retreat into the darkness of ignorance, and ignore the advent of the end.

a.text: I think, perhaps I've touched on the key to resolving this ultimate question—

spans.text: I think, perhaps I've touched on the key to resolving this ultimate question—

a.text: Use the language you and I created, {@nickname}.

spans.text: Use the language you and I created, {@nickname}.

a.text: 'It's time for this war to end, Dr. {@nickname}.'
'The purple flames ignited by that Draco have accelerated the course of the war. Once the Exemplars and the ducal alliance's troops push onto Nezzsalem's final stronghold—'
'Our goal of concluding this war will finally be within reach.'
'But... Dr. Kal'tsit, how long will it take for us to cover this short stretch?'
'There's no way to tell, Amiya.'

steps.name: Tired Wounded
steps.text: Originium...

steps.name: Tired Wounded
steps.text: Bloody Originium's really chopped this battleship in halves. I have to remain here and continue the fight with the local garrison...

steps.name: Tired Wounded
steps.text: Sorry, kid. I can't go on with you.

steps.name: Tough Infected
steps.text: This whole time we've seen nothing but ruins and dead... no garrisons at all.

steps.name: Tough Infected
steps.text: Also! Please don't call me kid! The monastery's already celebrated my coming-of-age!

steps.name: Tired Wounded
steps.text: Haha, you remind me of my daughter.

steps.name: Tired Wounded
steps.text: See the light shining up high there? That's part of Her Grace the Duke of Caster's Gloriana.

spans.text: See the light shining up high there? That's part of Her Grace the Duke of Caster's

steps.name: Tired Wounded
steps.text: That gun's still working, which means the news I got from the broadcast is true. My squad served the Duke, so I have to go back.

steps.name: Tough Infected
steps.text: But your wounds...

steps.name: Tired Wounded
steps.text: I can walk, since you helped patch me up.

steps.name: Tired Wounded
steps.text: But you, are you sure you want to go back to the city? It's the most polluted place there is. The active Originium in there will be the death of you.

steps.name: Tough Infected
steps.text: The Bishop told me that the kind person who saved me from the mines went through hell and back to deliver me all the way to the monastery.

steps.name: Tough Infected
steps.text: So I knew from an early age that salvation never comes without a cost.

steps.name: Tough Infected
steps.text: Don't worry about me. The clergy taught me many ways to keep myself safe.

steps.name: Tough Infected
steps.text: As long as I can save one more person, anyone, before I reach my end...

steps.name: Tired Wounded
steps.text: To be frank, this is the first time I've seen a cleric as devout as you... Your kind heart is the pride of Victoria.

steps.name: Tough Infected
steps.text: The Bishop says faith is not at all for pride or glory... the faithful believe with sincerity that good deeds will better this land...

steps.name: Tired Wounded
steps.text: Better this land...? Hah, maybe.

steps.name: Tired Wounded
steps.text: But anyway, thanks, little Cautus. For everything.

steps.name: Tired Wounded
steps.text: Could you help me out one last time, kid? If you make it back to the city, if my family... and my daughter's still there...

steps.name: Tired Wounded
steps.text: Please tell her that papa's always protected her.

The Victorian soldier struggles to raise his injured arm, and gives a non-standard salute to the Cautus, before calmly turning towards the distant wreckage and vanishing into the thicket of Originium.
The Cautus looks to the faint light emanating from the ship's gun and cannot help but to sigh.
Artillery sounds in the distance, and the tiny Cautus continues towards the city on the horizon—Londinium.

a.text: 'I hear the cannon fire too, Dr. {@nickname}. Madam Catherine's Crawler is already assaulting the Nachzehrer's front.'
'But will the war end once we beat them? And the innocents who've suffered... what will happen to them?'
'There's no way to save every single life in a war, Amiya. What we can do is help the Londiniers end this misery as soon as we can.'
'And that means the Nachzehrer aren't our ultimate problem.'

steps.name: Tough Infected
steps.text: Mary, Davey, please don't tell anyone else this kid is hiding here.

steps.name: Tough Infected
steps.text: I met him at the city walls, and he has nowhere to go. His parents are Londiniers, he said, and he met you two in the park a long while ago, yes?

steps.name: Disgusted Child
steps.text: I don't remember. You helped us, and I promised to help you. But he's not you!

steps.name: Tough Infected
steps.text: Thank you. He'll just hide here and won't run off or make a sound. I guarantee he won't give anyone a fright.

steps.name: Frightened Child
steps.text: (Nods quickly)

steps.name: Tough Infected
steps.text: I'll be back soon. I promised someone I'd find his daughter.

steps.name: Tough Infected
steps.text: It's impossible for me to protect you out there when there's so many hostiles—

steps.name: Tough Infected
steps.text: Sorry, I couldn't find anywhere better for you to settle down. I've helped quite a lot of people here though, so I trust these kids to keep you safe.
The tiny Sarkaz tugs sharply on the Cautus's arm, but touches the pointy Originium crystals instead.
He pulls back his hand on reflex.

steps.name: Frightened Child
steps.text: (softly) S-Sorry! When I was with my pa and ma... we rarely came in contact with Infected.

steps.name: Tough Infected
steps.text: ...I'll come back for you.

a.text: The Cautus is not gone for long.
When she arrives at the soldier's home as directed, there is nothing left.
But letters found in the ruin tell her the soldier's daughter joined a force rebelling against the Sarkaz in the city—the Exemplars.

It is a difficult journey for the Cautus as she returns to the refuge. When the Victorians joined forces to attack the Sarkaz front at the Palace of Westhaleg, Originium continued to spread throughout the city.
There are also those mad Sarkaz mercenaries wandering recklessly around, as if they've lost any semblance of humanity.
Her head hurts, from the city's terrible condition, but also from the horrific black crystals on her body.
'I might be nearing my end now, Father Bishop.'

steps.name: Tough Infected
steps.text: Excuse me... were you the troops who protected the people here from those mercenaries?

steps.name: Excited Soldier
steps.text: Yes. We have both Exemplar and ducal alliance troops in our squad, and we got a distress call while we were gearing up to enter the Palace.

steps.name: Excited Soldier
steps.text: Trust me, this mess will be over soon. Thank you too, for taking care of the kids and refugees.

steps.name: Excited Soldier
steps.text: Uh, are you looking for someone?
The Cautus shakes her head.

steps.name: Excited Soldier
steps.text: Right, we did mop up some of the devils hiding about. Probably here because their side's about to lose.

steps.name: Excited Soldier
steps.text: See you. We have to hurry on to the front.

steps.name: Tough Infected
steps.text: ...I didn't see that kid.

steps.name: Disgusted Child
steps.text: ...Follow me.
The child leads the Cautus through bunker after bunker within the factory, and the latter spots other refuge residents silently carrying away Sarkaz corpses.
They walk up to a pile of containers, and the child struggles but manages to push the messed up lid open.
The cowering Sarkaz child from before looks at them in fear.

steps.name: Disgusted Child
steps.text: She's here.

steps.name: Disgusted Child
steps.text: I promised you I'd help you, didn't I? It all happened so suddenly earlier, so this was the only place I could hide him.

steps.name: Silent Child
steps.text: But he can't stay here.

steps.name: Tough Infected
steps.text: On my way back, I met a group called Reunion. They can take him in.

steps.name: Reunion Member
steps.text: Don't worry, we'll take good care of that one—but what about you?

steps.name: Reunion Member
steps.text: Your Oripathy's serious... you should come with us too.

steps.name: Tough Infected
steps.text: I... still have some things to do.

steps.name: Reunion Member
steps.text: Alright, I won't force you. You remind me of a lot of my comrades.

steps.name: Reunion Member
steps.text: Here's some suppressants and protective gear. Good luck.

steps.name: Tough Infected
steps.text: ...You too.
Victorians advance in waves from afar towards the Nachzehrer King's last stand as life fades away.
That is not her war. She feels fear, and has no way of comprehending how these people overcome their fear of death, what keeps them pushing onward.
But she hopes to save people too, to continue numbly... one life after another.
...Even if it's all in vain.
She recalls the day she left the monastery. When she and the Bishop bid each other farewell by the riverside church.

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: What is faith, you ask?

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: Heheh... I traveled to Iberia in my youth, and saw with my own eyes how the lives of those around me collapsed during the Profound Silence, but that tenacious nation has never once yielded.

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: At first, I only admired the country's vitality, but as I lived my life, I came to realize...

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: That vitality, that is faith.

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: Who was there to teach me, or even the other Iberians, what path to take in life? Did anyone promise us we would surmount such a terrifying disaster?

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: No, but faced with calamity we always convince ourselves. Everything we go through is inevitably for something, suffering will eventually end, and we will enjoy a wonderful future.

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: That is faith.

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: Faith does not reside in scripture, nor in our prayers and hymns, but in our lives.

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: Faith is in our bodies and minds, in every heartbeat, in every breath. It is the source of all strength.

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: ...Only because we believe.

steps.name: Tough Infected
steps.text: Father Bishop, if it is as you say, that all suffering eventually ends, then where is our wonderful future you're talking about...?

steps.name: Tough Infected
steps.text: Father Bishop... I think... I've tried my best.
The Cautus collapses from exhaustion among the ruins, to the sounds of gunfire and cries from afar.
An intense pain reminds her of a cruel truth: this body has met its end.
She waves to those nearby whom she saved from death, staying alone in a wide open space far away from them.
Her body begins to disintegrate.

steps.name: Tough Infected
steps.text: ...I'm willing to believe...
The light caught in the Cautus's eyes begin to dim, until she sinks into endless night.
Then, she seems to see someone hold her almost shattered hand, and light begins to flow back into her eyes.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I think I heard the sound of an Infected disintegrating... again.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I could almost even see their final burst of light. Not too far from us.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: We've seen this happen too often lately...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Let's go, Doctor.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Doctor?

options: What exactly does... stasis within the Assimilated Universe mean?
Does that place we've been prevent even time from escaping?

steps.text: A surge of information rushes forward, trying to engulf him.
But Theresis does not budge.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: I finally see with my own eyes what great feat you've managed, Theresa.
He looks up at the tower standing in the void as falling fragments turn back into irregular information and return into the nothingness.
Theresis grabs a fragment that has drifted down to him, but it instantly turns to nothing in his palm.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: You opened this door for me, so I'll finish this last part of the journey in your stead, Theresa.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Once we Sarkaz seize the Originium that belongs to us, we shall for the first time hold the power to determine our own fate.
He grips the blade in his hand, and stares coldly at the large rhombus approaching him.
Then, he walks toward the crumbling tower. He knows well his opponent will be there.
Destroy anything, just to create a ladder. Theresa has left a path for him.

a.text: 'The myriad souls who never gave up resisting until they completely dissipated, did one last thing for the Sarkaz within the Originium—'
'They fought for a future where everyone has a right to survive, for the ones still alive.'
'Onward, everyone.'

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Just as always, my blade will cut our path forward. And you will lead the way.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: I never break my promises, Theresa—
He walks up the flight of stairs, towards the top of the nearly collapsed tower.
